title: Choose scenarios by the response they train, not just by the game tag
summary: A scenario transfers best when it teaches the same movement relationship and reaction pattern the game demands, even if the target motion or map does not look one-to-one identical.
why: Game-tagged scenarios can still train the wrong response if they reward a bad acquisition pattern or poor movement solution.
Motion mapping keeps the training anchored to what your hand actually needs to do in-game.
actions: Before keeping a scenario in the playlist, name the in-game response pattern it is supposed to improve.
If you cannot explain the motion relationship to your game, replace the scenario with one that trains the needed response more directly.
Prefer scenarios that teach the right micro-adjustment angles, pacing, and reaction pattern even if they do not look like the game.
avoid: Do not keep a scenario only because the title contains your game's name.

drills.label: Motion-mapped tracking drill
drills.reason: A motion-mapped drill helps transfer more than a superficially similar but mechanically wrong scenario.

evidence.claim: Useful scenarios copy the movement relationship and required response, not only the surface stimulus or game appearance.
evidence.excerpt: A good scenario copies the motion relationship and reflects the correct response to the stimulus in real games.
